init.description: Warning: Setting the refresh interval too low can cause your IP to be banned from Panasonic Cloud.

data_description.consumption_interval: How often to fetch energy consumption from the Panasonic cloud, in minutes. The cloud delivers new consumption data at most every 15 minutes (with some delay), so 15 is the lowest useful value; lower values only add load. Device state is refreshed every minute regardless of this setting.

app_version_rejected.title: Panasonic rejected the app version
app_version_rejected.description: Panasonic's servers no longer accept the app version that the Aquarea Smart Cloud integration announces, so logging in fails. Your username and password are not the problem and no re-authentication is needed. This is a change on Panasonic's side, which is usually fixed by updating the integration (and its aioaquarea-ng library): check for updates in HACS and restart Home Assistant. If you are already up to date, report it in the [issue tracker]({issues_url}). The integration keeps retrying, and this issue disappears by itself after a successful login.

pump_entities_changed.title: Pump status and direction entities changed
pump_entities_changed.description:
The pump status sensor of {entry_title} is now a binary sensor, so its entity ID moved to the binary_sensor domain:

{entities}

Update the automations, scripts, templates and dashboards that use the old entity IDs. The history of the old entity is not carried over; the recorder keeps it under the old entity ID.

The states of the pump direction sensor changed too: they are now lowercase (`idle`, `pump`, `water` instead of `IDLE`, `PUMP`, `WATER`). Update any condition or template that compares them. You can ignore this issue once you are done.

pump_entities_not_moved.title: Pump status sensor could not be moved
pump_entities_not_moved.description:
The pump status sensor of {entry_title} is now a binary sensor, but it could not be moved because the new entity ID is already used by another entity:

{entities}

Rename or remove the other entity, then reload the Aquarea Smart Cloud integration (or restart Home Assistant): the move is tried again on every setup, and this issue disappears once it has worked. Until then the new binary sensor gets a different entity ID.

The states of the pump direction sensor changed too: they are now lowercase (`idle`, `pump`, `water` instead of `IDLE`, `PUMP`, `WATER`). Update any condition or template that compares them.

direction_case_changed.title: Pump direction states are lowercase now
direction_case_changed.description: The states of the pump direction sensor of {entry_title} are now lowercase (`idle`, `pump`, `water` instead of `IDLE`, `PUMP`, `WATER`). Update any automation, script, template or dashboard condition that compares them. You can ignore this issue once you are done.
